title: Zugzwang of Zugzwangs
summary: Use checking moves to restrict the king, then make a quiet king move that removes the queen’s defensive squares.

nodes.question: How can the king help when the queens are far away?
nodes.explanation: The complete five-piece physical-board setup has White Kb5, Nd5 and Qg2 against Kc8 and Qf8. A quiet king move will matter after the checks.

branches.title: Check, then give Black the move
commentary: The complete five-piece physical-board setup has White Kb5, Nd5 and Qg2 against Kc8 and Qf8. A quiet king move will matter after the checks.
Qc2+ checks up the c-file, driving the king away from c8.
Kd8 chooses the illustrated route toward the kingside. Other king replies are separate variations.
Qc7+ brings the queen close and forces the king farther right.
Ke8 keeps Qf8 defending e7, where White threatens a protected queen mate. Checking immediately would let the king escape through f7.
Ka4 quietly takes a3 away from the black queen: Qa3 would otherwise keep e7 defended along a3-b4-c5-d6-e7. The king move preserves White’s mating threats.
Qf7 continues defending e7 along the seventh rank, but occupies the king’s f7 escape square. White changes the checking square instead.
Qc8# checks along the eighth rank. Nd5 covers e7, Qc8 covers d7/d8/f8, and Black’s own queen occupies f7.
branches.explanation: Qc8# checks along the eighth rank. Nd5 covers e7, Qc8 covers d7/d8/f8, and Black’s own queen occupies f7.

branches.title: Checking instead of improving the king
commentary: The complete five-piece physical-board setup has White Kb5, Nd5 and Qg2 against Kc8 and Qf8. A quiet king move will matter after the checks.
Qc2+ starts the forcing approach.
Kd8 moves right rather than toward the queenside.
Qc7+ continues the approach while maintaining coordination with the knight.
Ke8 reaches the critical diagram with the queen still on f8.
Qc8+ checks prematurely and gives away the forced win. The king has the f7 flight that ...Qf7 would have occupied.
Kf7 escapes. The exact remaining queen-and-knight versus queen position is drawn with best play; the selected line stops here.

branches.title: A tempting knight check loses the knight
commentary: The complete five-piece physical-board setup has White Kb5, Nd5 and Qg2 against Kc8 and Qf8. A quiet king move will matter after the checks.
Qc2+ begins the same checking approach.
Kd8 selects the main source route.
Qc7+ keeps the black king under pressure.
Ke8 reaches the position where a quiet move is needed.
Nf6+ gives up the win by exposing the knight to the queen on f8.
Qxf6 removes the knight and leaves a drawn queen ending. Black has a concrete response to the seemingly forcing check.

branches.title: Independent example against ...Kb8
commentary: An independently selected legal example illustrates the other direction of retreat, rather than claiming the sampled physical frames encode this exact move list.
Qc2+ checks along the file and asks Black which side to choose.
Kb8 goes toward the queenside, where White can coordinate queen and knight.
Qc7+ checks along the diagonal to b8 and cuts off c8.
Ka8 retreats to the corner in this representative line.
Nb6# checks a8 while Qc7 covers b8/b7 and Kb5 covers a6. The position is actual mate.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Nb6# checks a8 while Qc7 covers b8/b7 and Kb5 covers a6. The position is actual mate.

exercises.prompt: Why can Ka4 matter more than another check?
exercises.answer: Ka4 removes a3 as a defensive queen square while preserving the Qe7 mating threat. Black must change the arrangement; the illustrated Qf7 reply keeps e7 defended but blocks the king’s flight, allowing Qc8 mate.

startContext: The five-piece physical-board setup is reconstructed from multiple saved frames and the spoken Qc2 anchor. The illustrated main route and two checking errors are checked exactly; the ...Kb8 continuation is explicitly independent. No exhaustive defense tree is claimed.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
